newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end down on supply imbalance concerns.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end down on supply imbalance concerns.

text.p: Shares ended Tuesday's trading sharply lower, after sentiment was hijacked by fears of a supply and demand imbalance next month, brokers said.
The market ended down 13.76 points to a provisional 766.32.
"Everyone is getting more and more nervous," said Seung-wook Choe of Schroders Securities. "And the historically high margin loan levels are of real concern."

Margin loans are at about three trillion won, while customer deposits at brokerage houses lag behind at around 2.7 trillion. Analysts have said that 200-900 billion won in loans will have to be paid back in November.
There is an estimated 700 billion to 1.2 trillion won worth of new share supply coming into the market in November, from initial public offerings and rights issues.
Brokers said domestic institutions and foreign investors were mostly sidelined on Tuesday. Declining shares beat advancers 782 to 138, while 25.5 million shares changed hands.
Many brokers have forecast that the index could fall to around 750 before any improvement was seen. But more optimistic traders saw bargain hunting emerging to help the market.
"I think the index will recover to fluctuate in a 780 to 800 box range," said a Coryo Securities broker.
Despite the planned cut in reserve requirement ratios for local banks beginning November, investors feared that interest rates would not decrease, brokers said.

The reserve ratios will be cut from an average of 7.4 percent to 5.5 percent from November 8. But next month's huge new corporate bond issue schedule, about 3.1 trillion won worth, is expected to put upward pressure on yields.
South Korea's gross domestic product growth is expected to slow to around 6.5 percent next year from 6.8 percent, according to the Korea Development Institute.

Tae Hung Leather topped the most actives list, rising 600 won to 11,400. Choong Wae Pharmacy continued to attract interest after announcing it had developed a Hepatitis-B treatment drug. It gained 400 won to 40,500.
Blue chips were hit by active selling. Samsung Electronics fell 1,800 won to 59,100, while Korea Mobile Telecom shed 13,000 to 492,000.
December futures lost 0.50 of a point to 82.20, while the KOSPI 200 index shed 1.32 points to 79.93.
